 Validity of Section 11 Exemption on Belated ITR Filings: An In-Depth Analysis of the ITAT Delhi Ruling
 Income Tax 24 Oct 2026 10 min read
 Validity of Section 11 Exemption on Belated ITR Filings: An In-Depth Analysis of the ITAT Delhi Ruling
 The intersection of procedural compliance and substantive tax exemptions for charitable institutions has long been a subject of extensive litigation. A recurring point of friction between the revenue authorities and charitable trusts revolves around the denial of exemption benefits when income tax returns are filed after the initial due date but within the extended statutory timeframes.
 In a significant judicial development, the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Delhi Bench ‘SMC’, delivered a crucial order in the case of Conference of Religious India Vs Ward Exemption 1(3) . The ruling, pronounced on 13 October 2022, under ITA No. 2161/Del/2022, addresses whether a charitable entity holding registration under Section 12A of the Income-tax Act, 1961 can be stripped of its exemption under Section 11 solely because its return of income was filed a few days beyond the extended deadline prescribed under Section 139(1) , yet comfortably within the permissible window for a belated return under Section 139(4) .
 This article provides a comprehensive examination of the tribunal's decision, the statutory framework governing charitable exemptions, the relevance of Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) circulars, and the broader implications for the non-profit sector.
 1. The Statutory Framework Governing Charitable Exemptions
 To appreciate the nuances of the tribunal's ruling, it is essential to understand the legislative provisions that govern the taxation of charitable and religious institutions.
 (i) The Mandate of Section 11 and Section 12A
 Under the Income-tax Act, 1961 , Section 11 provides a substantive exemption on income derived from property held under trust wholly for charitable or religious purposes, subject to certain application and accumulation conditions. For an entity to avail of this benefit, it must be registered under Section 12A (or Section 12AA as applicable).
 A critical amendment was introduced via the insertion of Section 12A(1)(ba) , which mandated an additional prerequisite for claiming the exemption. It required that the person in receipt of the income must furnish the return of income within the time allowed under Section 139 .
 (ii) The Interplay of Section 139 Subsections
 Section 139 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 is a comprehensive code dealing with the filing of returns.
 Section 139(1) stipulates the standard due dates for filing the original return of income.
 Section 139(4) provides a grace period, allowing an assessee to file a belated return before the end of the relevant assessment year or before the completion of the assessment, whichever is earlier.
 Section 139(4A) specifically directs entities claiming exemption under Section 11 and Section 12 to file their returns if their total income exceeds the basic exemption limit.
 The core dispute in many assessments arises when the revenue department interprets "time allowed under Section 139 " strictly as the due date under Section 139(1) , thereby automatically denying exemptions during the computerized processing of returns if filed under Section 139(4) .
 2. Factual Matrix of the Dispute
 The assessee, a charitable institution duly registered under Section 12A of the Income-tax Act, 1961 , sought exemption under Section 11 for the Assessment Year 2020-21.
